title: Cate's First Day
description: Help Cate, a learning robot on an exchange year in Glasgow, write her first diary entry. Practise eight travel words and phrases, read about her new flatmates and use was and were.

competencies.description: Practice focus: find information in a short English story.
Practice focus: write three clear diary sentences from Cate's point of view and check them yourself.
Practice focus: understand eight travel words and phrases and use them in writing.
Practice focus: use was/were in statements, a negative sentence and a yes/no question.

learningObjectives: I can understand eight travel words and phrases and find key information in Cate's story.
I can help Cate write three diary sentences using at least three different target words or phrases and at least two correct forms of was/were.

blocks.title: Help Cate!
blocks.body:
Cate is the EveryCate learning robot. She is an exchange student at the **University of Glasgow** in Scotland. On her first day, she has a problem with her screen and meets two new flatmates: Calum and Timo. Help her write **three diary sentences about yesterday**.

**Your learning goals:**

- I can understand eight travel words and phrases and find key information in Cate's story.
- I can help Cate write three diary sentences using at least three different target words or phrases and at least two correct forms of was/were.

Read and write at your own pace. You can do every activity by reading and writing.

blocks.title: Travel words
blocks.body:
Read the eight target words. Learn **railway station** and **over there** as whole phrases.

**journey** – eine Reise

**railway station** – Bahnhof

**ticket** – Fahrkarte

**passenger** – eine Person, die in einem Verkehrsmittel mitreist

**friendly** – freundlich

**nearby** – in der Nähe

**over there** – dort drüben

**diary** – Tagebuch

Choose one answer for each question. After you check your answers, read the explanations. If you make a mistake, read the hint, look at this word bank if you need help and try again.

blocks.title: Four meanings
blocks.intro: Choose the matching German meaning for each word. Choose one answer for each question.

questions.explanation: Hint: A journey is a trip from one place to another. A ticket is what you need for the trip. Think about the difference and try again.
Hint: Trains stop here. People get on and off trains here. Learn railway station as one phrase. Read the choices and try again.

questions.prompt: What does **ticket** mean in this module?
questions.explanation: Hint: You need a ticket to travel on a train. It can be on paper or on a screen. Think about what you need for the trip and try again.

options.text: eine Person, die in einem Verkehrsmittel mitreist
ein Ort, an dem Züge halten

questions.explanation: Hint: A passenger is a person who travels in a car, bus, train or another vehicle. Look for the person in the choices and try again.

blocks.title: Four gaps
blocks.intro: Which word or phrase fits the gap? These are short practice situations. Cate’s story comes next.

questions.explanation: Hint: Her smile and her welcome show that she is kind. The word friendly fits. Read the whole sentence and try again.

questions.prompt: The café is not far away. It is ___.
questions.explanation: Hint: Nearby means not far away. Look for the word that tells you how close the café is and try again.

questions.prompt: Look across the street! The bus stop is ___.
questions.explanation: Hint: Someone is pointing to a place across the street. Over there means dort drüben. Learn both words together and try again.

questions.prompt: My ___ is a book with a page for each day. It is for my thoughts.
questions.explanation: Hint: A diary is a book for your thoughts and the things in your day. Think about the kind of book and try again.

blocks.title: Cate’s first day
blocks.body:
**Read Cate’s story. You can look back at it when you answer the questions.**

Hi! I'm Cate, a learning robot. I am an exchange student at the University of Glasgow. This is my first week in Scotland.

Yesterday my journey was long. I was a passenger on a train. My ticket was on my screen. At a small railway station near Glasgow, my screen was dark. No ticket and no map!

Two students, Calum and Timo, were there. They were friendly. The other passengers were friendly, too. Timo was next to me with a map on his phone.

Calum is from Scotland. Timo is an exchange student from Germany. He studies engineering. They are my flatmates! Our student accommodation is nearby. Look, it is over there, across the street.

Now I am in my room. My room has its own bathroom. We share a kitchen. Calum's expensive bike is in his room because he is afraid of thieves. My screen is bright again, and my diary is open. Can you help me write about yesterday?

**Word help:** yesterday = gestern; screen = Bildschirm; dark / bright = dunkel / hell; exchange student = Austauschstudent/in; flatmates = Mitbewohner; student accommodation = Studierendenwohnheim; across the street = auf der anderen Straßenseite; engineering = Ingenieurwesen; its own bathroom = ein eigenes Badezimmer; share = teilen; expensive = teuer; afraid of thieves = hat Angst vor Dieben.

blocks.title: Understand the scene
blocks.intro: Choose one answer for each question. You can find every answer in the story. If you make a mistake, read the feedback, look at the story again and have another try.

questions.explanation: Cate says, “Yesterday my journey was long.” The answer is long. Look for journey in the story when you try again.

questions.prompt: Which two students were at the railway station with Cate?
questions.explanation: The story says, “Two students, Calum and Timo, were there.” Rowan and Sam are not in this story. Read the paragraph after the screen problem and try again.

questions.prompt: Is the student accommodation nearby or far away?
questions.explanation: “Our student accommodation is nearby.” It is close. “Over there, across the street” tells you where it is. Read that paragraph and try again.

blocks.title: Talk about yesterday
blocks.body:
You know **am, is, are** for now. Use these forms of **to be** to talk about **yesterday**:

| Person or thing | Now | Yesterday |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | am | **was** |
| he / she / it | is | **was** |
| you / we / they | are | **were** |

**A statement:** Person or thing + was/were + the rest of the sentence.

- Now I **am** in my room. Yesterday I **was** on a train.
- Calum and Timo = they: They **were** at the station.

**A negative sentence:** Put **not** directly after was/were.

- was not = **wasn’t**: My screen **wasn’t** bright at the station.
- were not = **weren’t**: Calum and Timo **weren’t** at home. They were at the station.

**A yes/no question:** Was/Were + person or thing + the rest of the sentence + a question mark.

- They **were** friendly. → **Were** they friendly?
- Answer: Yes, they were.

Now do the next three activities. If you make a mistake, use the table and try again.

blocks.title: was or were?
blocks.intro: Type **was** or **were**. If you make a mistake, remember: Cate = she; Calum and Timo = they. Look at the table and try again.
blocks.text:
Yesterday Cate {{1}} a passenger.
Yesterday, Calum and Timo {{2}} at the railway station.

blocks.title: Make it negative
blocks.intro: Make this sentence negative to match the story: **Her screen was bright at the station.** Complete the sentence below. You can use the short form or the full form. Hint: her screen = it; put **not** after the correct past form. Then try again.
blocks.text: Her screen {{1}} bright at the station.

blocks.title: Ask a question
blocks.intro: Type **Was** or **Were**. If you make a mistake, remember: Calum and Timo = they. In a yes/no question, was or were comes first. Look at the table and try again.

blocks.title: Write Cate’s diary
blocks.intro: Help Cate with your own text. Open the hint for a word bank and sentence starters if you need help. After writing, compare your text with the examples and check it yourself.

tasks.prompt:
Write **three English sentences about yesterday as Cate** in the answer box. Use **I** or **my** when Cate writes about herself.

Use **at least three different target words or phrases** and **at least two correct forms of was/were**. You can use the same form more than once if it fits the sentence. railway station and over there each count as **one** phrase. Your sentences must match Cate’s story.

Then open the example answer and check your work. Improve your text if you need to.
tasks.hint:
**journey** – eine Reise

**railway station** – Bahnhof

**ticket** – Fahrkarte

**passenger** – eine Person, die in einem Verkehrsmittel mitreist

**friendly** – freundlich

**nearby** – in der Nähe

**over there** – dort drüben

**diary** – Tagebuch

**Sentence starters:** Yesterday my journey … / I … a passenger … / I … at the railway station. / Calum and Timo … / My screen …

**Forms:** I / he / she / it **was**; you / we / they **were**. **wasn't = was not**, **weren't = were not**.

Read the story again if you need help. Choose three things about yesterday. A sentence about Cate’s room today does not tell us about yesterday.
tasks.solution:
**One possible answer:**

My journey was long. I was at the railway station. Calum and Timo were friendly.

This example uses three different target words or phrases: **journey**, **railway station**, **friendly**. It uses **was**, **was** and **were** correctly.

**Other clear answers that match the story are also correct.** For example: Yesterday I was a passenger on a train. My ticket was on my screen. The other passengers were friendly.

**Check your work:**

- Are there three English sentences?
- Do I write as Cate, using I or my, about yesterday?
- Does my information match the story?
- Can I find at least three different target words or whole phrases? Passengers is the plural of passenger: it counts as the same target word.
- Do I use was/were correctly at least twice? Using was twice is fine if it fits both sentences.
- Does each sentence start with a capital letter and end with a punctuation mark?

Your diary can be different from the examples. Use them to check your work. Ask your teacher if you are not sure.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.intro: Try these two questions without the word bank first. These are **new practice situations, not extra facts about the story**. If you make a mistake, remember: passengers = they. The word bank can help with the word in the second sentence. Then try again.
blocks.text:
Yesterday, two friendly passengers {{1}} nearby.
I write about my day in my {{2}}.

tasks.prompt:
Think about the travel words and your three diary sentences. Write **one** of these three choices in the answer box:

- I can do this already
- I did it with help
- I want to practise this more

You can add a word or a form you want to practise again. Every choice is OK.
tasks.hint: Think about your work: Can you choose the words and was/were on your own? Do the word bank or examples help? Do you need another try?
tasks.solution: There is no right or wrong choice here. For more practice, repeat a word activity or improve a diary sentence. This module helps you practise reading and writing.
